items.description: Analyze repository structure and tooling capabilities
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/phase1/repo_analysis.md listing all modules (.archivara/concept_evolve.py, .archivara/semantic_scholar.py, .opencode/ agents and tools), their purposes, API capabilities, and how they connect in the multi-agent pipeline. Confirm concept_evolve supports evolve/probe/reframe/walk commands and semantic_scholar supports search/citations/references/recommend/graph/bibtex.

items.description: Number-theoretic analysis of 668 and its factorizations
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/phase1/number_theory_668.md: (1) 668 = 4 * 167, where 167 is prime and 167 ≡ 3 mod 4; (2) all factorizations of 668 as products of integers >=2; (3) analysis of 167 as a Paley prime (q ≡ 3 mod 4 gives Paley Type I of order q+1=168); (4) feasibility of Kronecker product routes (e.g., H_668 cannot be H_a ⊗ H_b since 668=4*167 and 167 is prime); (5) residues and quadratic character properties of GF(167).
items.notes: 668 is the smallest open case of the Hadamard conjecture as of 2025. 167 is prime, 167 ≡ 3 mod 4. Direct tensor decomposition is impossible since 167 is prime and has no useful Hadamard-order factors.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive literature review on Hadamard matrices of order 668 using web search and Semantic Scholar
items.acceptance_criteria: At least 15 relevant papers cited in sources.bib with full BibTeX entries. Must include: (1) Eliahou 2025 '64-modular Hadamard matrix of order 668'; (2) Cati & Pasechnik 2024 'A database of constructions of Hadamard matrices' (arXiv:2411.18897); (3) Djokovic & Kotsireas work on GS difference families; (4) Balonin & Djokovic 2018 on propus construction for symmetric Hadamard matrices; (5) Seberry & Yamada survey on Hadamard sequences and block designs; (6) Kharaghani & Tayfeh-Rezaie on classification and construction; (7) Eliahou & Kervaire 2001/2005 on modular Hadamard matrices; (8) Horadam 2007 textbook; (9) at least 6 additional relevant papers covering Williamson matrices, orthogonal designs, supplementary difference sets, T-matrices, or Baumert-Hall arrays.
items.notes: Use semantic_scholar tool for search/citations/references/graph commands. Use websearch for finding recent preprints on arXiv.

items.description: Map all known construction methods and their applicability to order 668
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/phase1/construction_methods.md a table of at least 10 construction methods with columns: Method, Required Input, Applicable to n=668?, Key Constraints, Key References. Must cover: Sylvester, Paley I & II, Williamson, Williamson-type, Goethals-Seidel array, propus array, Baumert-Hall arrays, orthogonal designs (OD), supplementary difference sets (SDS), T-matrices/T-sequences, product constructions, and doubling/tripling lemmas. Each entry must cite at least one paper from sources.bib.

items.description: Delegate concept-tree exploration of cross-domain approaches to Hadamard matrix construction
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve evolve with topic 'Hadamard matrix construction for order 668 via algebraic, combinatorial, and computational methods'. Verify that results/concept_evolve/tree/ contains at least 10 concept folders, each with concept.json, literature.json, and README.md. Synthesize a summary in results/phase1/concept_tree_summary.md listing all concept nodes, bridge chains, and top-3 most promising cross-domain connections.
items.notes: This is the subagent delegation item for Phase 1. The concept_evolve tool will invoke a sub-agent to generate concept cards spanning algebraic, combinatorial, coding-theoretic, and computational domains.

items.description: Identify and document the current frontier: why 668 remains open
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/phase1/frontier_analysis.md: (1) SageMath covers all orders ≤664 (Cati & Pasechnik); (2) 668=4*167 is the smallest open case; (3) Williamson matrices of order 167 are unknown (167 is in the list of hard primes); (4) no GS difference family in Z_167 with four blocks yielding Hadamard matrix is known; (5) the 64-modular result by Eliahou is the best approximation; (6) list of the 13 hard primes v<500 where 4v Hadamard matrix is unknown: {167, 179, 223, 251, 283, 311, 347, 359, 419, 443, 479, 487, 491}. Cite at least 5 papers from sources.bib.

items.description: Implement Hadamard matrix verification infrastructure
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/hadamard_utils.py with functions: (1) is_hadamard(M) — checks H*H^T = nI for ±1 matrix; (2) orthogonality_defect(M) — computes ||H*H^T - nI||_F (Frobenius norm); (3) modular_check(M, m) — checks if H*H^T ≡ nI mod m; (4) row_inner_products(M) — returns matrix of all pairwise row dot products; (5) near_hadamard_score(M) — composite metric combining orthogonality defect and entry constraint satisfaction. All functions must include unit tests in tests/test_hadamard_utils.py that pass against known Hadamard matrices of orders 4, 8, 12, 20 (Paley construction).

items.description: Implement baseline construction methods as reference implementations
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/constructions/ directory with: (1) paley.py — Paley Type I (for q ≡ 3 mod 4 prime power, constructs order q+1) and Type II (for q ≡ 1 mod 4); (2) sylvester.py — Kronecker/tensor construction for powers of 2; (3) williamson.py — Williamson array from four symmetric circulant matrices; (4) goethals_seidel.py — GS array from four circulant blocks and the back-circulant matrix R. Each must produce a verified Hadamard matrix for at least 2 test orders. Verify Paley I produces H_168 (since 167 ≡ 3 mod 4 is prime).

items.description: Implement Goethals-Seidel difference family search framework for Z_167
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gs_difference_family.py that: (1) represents cyclic difference families (v; k1, k2, k3, k4; lambda) in Z_v; (2) computes the development of a difference family into four circulant matrices; (3) plugs into the GS array to produce a 4v × 4v candidate matrix; (4) evaluates the orthogonality defect of the resulting matrix. Demonstrate it works correctly by reproducing a known GS construction for a smaller prime (e.g., v=47 or v=59). Document the search space size for v=167 with four blocks.

items.description: Delegate literature-graph mining for product and doubling constructions applicable near order 668
items.acceptance_criteria: Use the literature-graph-miner subagent (or semantic_scholar graph command) starting from Cati & Pasechnik 2024 and Djokovic's GS papers to build a citation graph of depth 2. Identify at least 5 papers that use product constructions, doubling lemmas, or asymptotic existence results that could reach order 668 from known Hadamard matrices. Save the citation graph as results/phase2/citation_graph.json and a synthesis document as results/phase2/product_routes.md listing each viable route with its prerequisites.
items.notes: This is the subagent delegation item for Phase 2.

items.description: Establish metrics dashboard for tracking construction attempts
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/metrics.py with: (1) log_attempt(method, params, defect, time) — logs each construction attempt to results/metrics/attempts.jsonl; (2) best_so_far() — returns the attempt with lowest orthogonality defect; (3) summary_stats() — returns counts per method, average defect, best defect, total time. Create results/metrics/ directory. Verify with at least 5 logged dummy attempts.

items.description: Investigate the propus construction for symmetric Hadamard matrix of order 668
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/constructions/propus.py implementing the propus array [A B B D; B D -A -B; B -A -D B; D -B B -A] where A, B, D are symmetric circulant ±1 matrices of order 167. Document in results/phase3/propus_analysis.md: (1) the algebraic constraints on A, B, D (the Propus equation: A² + 2B² + D² = 4*167*I); (2) connection to supplementary difference sets in Z_167; (3) feasibility analysis including search space reduction via multiplier automorphisms (since 167 is prime, the multiplier group is large). Reference Balonin & Djokovic 2018 and Seberry 2014 propus papers from sources.bib.
items.notes: The propus construction has been very successful for constructing symmetric Hadamard matrices of previously unknown orders (268, 412, 436, 604 by Balonin & Djokovic 2018).

items.description: Explore Goethals-Seidel construction with mixed symmetric/skew base blocks for v=167
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/constructions/gs_mixed.py implementing GS difference families in Z_167 where base blocks can be symmetric, skew, or mixed (following Djokovic & Kotsireas 2018). Document in results/phase3/gs_mixed_analysis.md: (1) enumeration of the different symmetry types (SSSS, SSSK, SSKS, etc.); (2) algebraic constraints for each type (the power spectral density conditions); (3) exploitation of the multiplicative group structure of GF(167) to reduce search space; (4) connection to Legendre symbol and quadratic residues of 167. Must cite Djokovic & Kotsireas arXiv:1802.00556.

items.description: Investigate orthogonal designs and Baumert-Hall arrays targeting order 668
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/od_bh_analysis.md documenting: (1) which full orthogonal designs OD(4n; s1,...,sk) with s1+...+sk = 4n can produce order 668 Hadamard matrices when instantiated with appropriate ±1 sequences; (2) known Baumert-Hall arrays of relevant orders and whether any can be combined with known sequences to reach 668; (3) analysis of OD(16; s1,...,s9)-based constructions (Kotsireas & Koukouvinos 2008); (4) whether 668 = 4 * 167 admits a factorization through any known OD family. Cite at least 3 papers from sources.bib.

items.description: Delegate concept-tree probe on the specific bottleneck: constructing four circulant blocks in Z_167 satisfying the GS/propus power spectral density condition
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve probe with problem description targeting the specific PSD constraint: 'Given Z_167, find four ±1 sequences a,b,c,d of length 167 whose periodic autocorrelation functions sum to 4*167*delta(0). This is the Goethals-Seidel or Propus PSD condition.' Results must appear in results/concept_evolve/tree/ with at least 5 new concept cards. Synthesize in results/phase3/psd_probe_synthesis.md listing cross-domain analogies (e.g., from signal processing, coding theory, or optimization) and at least 2 novel algorithmic strategies suggested by the probe.
items.notes: This is the subagent delegation item for Phase 3. The PSD (power spectral density) condition is the fundamental constraint: |A(ω)|² + |B(ω)|² + |C(ω)|² + |D(ω)|² = 4n for all n-th roots of unity ω.

items.description: Explore algebraic number theory approach: ideal factorization in Z[ζ_167] and Galois descent
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/phase3/algebraic_approach.md: (1) the group ring formulation of GS/Williamson equations in Z[Z_167]; (2) factorization of 4*167 in the cyclotomic ring Z[ζ_167] where ζ_167 is a primitive 167th root of unity; (3) since 167 is prime, analysis of the structure of the ideal class group of Q(ζ_167); (4) whether known ideal factorizations can constrain the search for difference families; (5) connection to the Legendre symbol χ_167 and Gauss sums. Must reference at least 2 papers from sources.bib on algebraic approaches to Hadamard matrices.

items.description: Investigate modular lifting strategy: from Eliahou's 64-modular result toward a true Hadamard matrix
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/phase3/modular_lifting.md: (1) summary of Eliahou's 64-modular Hadamard matrix of order 668 (H*H^T ≡ 668*I mod 64); (2) the sequence of modular improvements: 12-modular (Marrero-Butson 1972), 32-modular (Eliahou-Kervaire 2001), 64-modular (Eliahou 2025); (3) analysis of whether a p-adic lifting or Hensel-type strategy could push the modulus higher (128, 256, ...); (4) relationship between modular Golay pairs/quadruples and the modular construction; (5) feasibility assessment of approaching a true Hadamard matrix (modulus → ∞) via iterated lifting. Cite Eliahou 2025 and Eliahou-Kervaire 2001/2005.
items.notes: The modular approach is the only known method that has produced any structured ±1 matrix of order 668 with partial Hadamard-like properties.

items.description: Explore cocyclic Hadamard matrices and group-developed constructions for order 668
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/phase3/cocyclic_analysis.md: (1) definition of cocyclic Hadamard matrices over a group G of order 668/1=668; (2) candidate groups of order 668 (668 = 4 * 167, possible groups: Z_668, Z_4 × Z_167, D_334, etc.); (3) analysis of which groups G have a cocycle f: G×G → {±1} producing a Hadamard matrix; (4) connection to the second cohomology group H²(G, Z_2); (5) feasibility of cocyclic search for the dihedral or semi-direct product groups. Cite Horadam 2007 and at least 1 paper on cocyclic constructions.

items.description: Execute targeted search for propus difference families in Z_167 using multiplier reduction
items.acceptance_criteria: Run the propus construction search (from item_012) with multiplier automorphism reduction. Log all attempts via the metrics system (item_011). Document in results/phase4/propus_search_log.md: (1) multiplier group used and its order; (2) search space size before and after reduction; (3) number of candidates evaluated; (4) best orthogonality defect achieved; (5) total computation time. If a valid propus family is found, save it as results/phase4/propus_family_167.json and verify the resulting 668×668 matrix is Hadamard.

items.description: Execute GS mixed-type difference family search for v=167 with algebraic constraints
items.acceptance_criteria: Run the GS mixed-type search (from item_013) incorporating the Legendre symbol structure of GF(167). Log all attempts via the metrics system. Document in results/phase4/gs_search_log.md: (1) symmetry types explored; (2) algebraic constraints applied (PSD conditions, multiplier orbits); (3) best orthogonality defect per symmetry type; (4) total candidates and time. If a valid GS family is found, save as results/phase4/gs_family_167.json.

items.description: Attempt indirect/product constructions combining known Hadamard matrices to reach order 668
items.acceptance_criteria: Based on results from item_010 and item_014, implement and test at least 3 indirect routes to order 668. For each route, document in results/phase4/indirect_routes.md: (1) the construction chain (e.g., H_a ⊗ ... combined with doubling lemma); (2) whether all prerequisites are satisfiable; (3) outcome (success/failure with reason). Compare against routes identified in the literature review (Phase 1). Even negative results must be documented with clear mathematical justification for why the route fails.

items.description: Delegate concept-tree walk to synthesize experimental findings across all attempted methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve walk with seed keywords from the most promising experimental results (e.g., 'propus', 'Goethals-Seidel', 'modular lifting', 'difference family'). Produce results/phase4/concept_walk_synthesis.md that: (1) traces concept paths through the tree; (2) identifies which concept bridges were validated or invalidated by experiments; (3) proposes at least 2 refined strategies combining insights from multiple concept domains. This should guide any follow-up experiments.
items.notes: This is the subagent delegation item for Phase 4.

items.description: Evaluate all results against prior work and the 64-modular benchmark
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/evaluation.md comparing: (1) best orthogonality defect achieved vs Eliahou's 64-modular result; (2) for each construction method attempted, comparison of search efficiency against published results (cite from sources.bib); (3) table of all construction attempts with method, parameters, defect, modular level achieved, and time; (4) ranking of methods by promise for future work. Must reference at least 5 papers from sources.bib for comparison.

items.description: Synthesize all findings into a comprehensive research report
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/report/hadamard_668_report.md with sections: (1) Abstract; (2) Introduction & Background (citing at least 8 papers from sources.bib); (3) Number-Theoretic Analysis of 668; (4) Construction Methods Investigated (with mathematical details); (5) Experimental Results (tables, defect metrics, timings); (6) Novel Insights & Cross-Domain Connections (from concept_evolve); (7) Comparison with Prior Work; (8) Conclusions & Future Directions; (9) Full Bibliography. Report must be at least 3000 words with proper mathematical notation.

items.description: Generate visualization figures for key results
items.acceptance_criteria: Create at least 4 figures in figures/ directory: (1) figures/construction_method_comparison.png — bar chart of orthogonality defects by method; (2) figures/concept_tree_graph.png — visualization of the concept evolution tree with bridge edges highlighted; (3) figures/search_convergence.png — plot of best defect vs. computation time for each search method; (4) figures/modular_progression.png — visualization of modular Hadamard hierarchy (12→32→64→? for order 668). All figures must have axis labels, titles, and legends.

items.description: Delegate final concept-tree reframe to identify unexplored avenues for future work
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve reframe with problem 'Construct a Hadamard matrix of order 668 = 4*167 given that all standard methods (Williamson, GS, propus, product) have not yet succeeded.' The reframe must produce mappings across at least 8 distinct domains (e.g., signal processing, algebraic geometry, quantum information, graph theory, optimization, machine learning, coding theory, number theory). Save output in results/concept_evolve/tree/ and synthesize in results/phase5/reframe_future_directions.md with at least 5 concrete, actionable research directions not previously attempted.
items.notes: This is the subagent delegation item for Phase 5.

items.description: Final verification of sources.bib completeness and correctness
items.acceptance_criteria: Verify sources.bib contains: (1) at least 15 BibTeX entries; (2) every entry has required fields (author, title, year, and either journal/booktitle/howpublished); (3) every paper cited in the report (item_024) has a corresponding entry; (4) no duplicate entries; (5) entries are sorted alphabetically by cite key. Run a BibTeX syntax check (or manual validation) and fix any errors. Document the final count and any corrections in results/phase5/bib_verification.md.

items.description: Create reproducibility documentation and archive all experimental artifacts
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/README.md documenting: (1) directory structure of all results; (2) how to reproduce each experiment (commands, parameters, expected runtime); (3) software dependencies and versions used; (4) hardware/environment specifications; (5) mapping from rubric items to result files. Ensure all JSON/JSONL files in results/ are valid. Create results/phase5/artifact_manifest.json listing every output file with its rubric item reference, creation date, and size.
